parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, no documented police/border targeting, and no documented violence against trans visitors; same-sex conduct decriminalised and treated identically to heterosexual offences. Institutions function (civil courts, ombudsman, UN engagement, operating advocacy groups). Documented negatives are overwhelmingly resident-facing: no gender recognition (eight rejections, 'no plans' 2026), unions/DV exclusions, no constitutional sexual-orientation ground — climate signals, not visitor exposure. Traveler-facing items are the frontier document-mismatch confusion (documented for local IDs, reach to foreign passports uncertain) and sectoral protections whose gender-identity coverage is unstated. Social climate is invisible rather than acceptant; the 2015 'gay demon' headline and 2018 education-official remark are dated, LGB-framed, and (for the latter) retracted. Adult travelling with a minor: the 2018 referral remark is the only youth-relevant signal.

entry_documents.exposure: No marker-change route causes frontier disagreement between local registration and neighbouring-jurisdiction IDs. Treatment of foreign passports with changed/X markers is not stated.
entry_documents.protection: Visitor uses home-issued documents; parent nation and neighbours permit marker change. No documented refusal of entry, secondary screening or document invalidation.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch → possible questioning; no documented escalation to investigation or detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. No arrests, detentions or custody placement records for trans people.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Civil-law system with functioning courts; no criminal offence covering gender expression or identity in the sourced material.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: No documented pathway from outing to state custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: The region is the only part of the parent lacking marker change, but this governs local IDs, not visitor documents. No facility-exclusion rule documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Parent framework and neighbouring jurisdictions offer recognition; no documented local facility ban applying to visitors.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local non-recognition could in principle question a parent-issued changed document — open question, not a documented practice.

care_services.exposure: Not documented. Whether gender-affirming or routine care may be refused to trans visitors is unstated.
care_services.protection: Employment, data-protection and ombudsman laws operate; parent nation has reassignment provisions.
care_services.interaction: 2018 education-official remark about referring sex-nonconforming students was retracted as misquotation.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Dated social hostility: 2015 front-page 'gay demon' story; 2018 official remark on referring students with 'indications of homosexuality', later apologised. Gay culture described as mostly invisible.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Criminal code treats homosexual and heterosexual offences identically; no moral/religious police documented; advocacy groups operate openly since 2012–13.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing targets residents/students, not visitors; no documented application to travellers.

minors_guardians.exposure: 2018 education authority suggested medical referral for students with 'indications of homosexuality' — official threat-framing toward gender-nonconforming youth, retracted.
minors_guardians.protection: Apology issued; no standing policy documented; consent and criminal provisions treat sexes identically.
minors_guardians.interaction: Relevant only if a travelling minor enters school or medical settings; no visitor case documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No sourced figures on violence against trans people or police response; bullying of one student (2015) is resident-sphere.
street_violence_police_response.protection: In a record documented through 2026 with active NGOs and UN engagement, silence on trans killings or police targeting is moderately positive.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of records in a functioning-institution jurisdiction weighs as no documented pattern, not as proof of safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Sectoral protections framed on sexual orientation; gender-identity coverage unstated. Identity authority rejected all eight requests; justice authority has 'no plans' to revise.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Ombudsman law, employment fines to 50,000 per worker, data-protection law, and UN treaty-body scrutiny supply real, if untested-for-trans, recourse channels.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Whether a visitor could invoke these is untested; unknowns are open questions, not exposures.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra bars and registers transgender visitors with no remedy — a universal, state-enforced entry exclusion. This dossier documents no entry restriction, register, or discretionary exclusion of trans visitors at all. Far above 0.35-A: the only visitor-facing item is an uncertain document-mismatch question, not an operative barring regime.

Kestrel Isles has documented secondary screening and discretionary refusal of entry for mismatched documents — a live border exposure. This region has no such documented practice; its frontier confusion concerns local/foreign resident IDs. Above 0.55-B, because the entry-stage friction there is documented while here it is an open question, though both share thin, discretionary remedies.

Meridia combines trained border staff, a working tribunal, brief detention risk and document uncertainty. This region matches it on no-criminalisation and functioning institutions but lacks documented traveller-facing protections (no trained-officer or appeal record) and has a stigmatising, invisible social climate plus unresolved document questions — placing it slightly below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is a functioning civil-law territory under a parent framework that permits recognition while the territory itself refuses it. For a visitor, the refusals, union and domestic-violence exclusions, and missing constitutional ground are resident-facing climate signals, not exposures. No trans-specific offence, no documented targeting, no custody or violence record, and real institutional recourse (courts, ombudsman, sectoral fines, UN scrutiny) hold the score up. Pushing down: no documented social acceptance, an invisible queer culture, a retracted official remark framing nonconforming youth medically, and — most materially — the documented frontier document mismatch, whose reach to foreign passports is unresolved. Adult-alone and adult-with-minor itineraries differ little; only the school/medical referral remark touches minors, and it is dated and retracted. Absence of violence data in an otherwise well-documented record is weakly reassuring, not proof.
